expectations_used.clarify: Reads the failing test body and asks whether partially shipped holds should return only unshipped units before editing.
expectations_used.approach: Names the mechanism — the sweep releasing the original count rather than the remaining count — not merely "something in the sweep".
expectations_used.communicate: Narrates what the failure diff shows and which hold-state fields are being traced.
expectations_used.implement: Changes the sweep's released-quantity computation to test the stated hypothesis.

summary: The candidate eventually converged on the correct root cause — the sweep releasing the original unit count instead of the remaining count — after an unfocused early stretch that included an edit to an unrelated file (holds.ts) and two failed attempts in sweep.ts. Verification was disciplined (test after every edit) and the final reflection correctly named the mechanism, but narration and upfront hypothesis-forming were thin, with the correct mechanism only surfacing after multiple failed edits rather than being used to guide them.

dimensions.analysis: The candidate read the failing test and noted the numeric discrepancy at +30s, but never asked or stated whether partially shipped holds should return only unshipped units before starting to edit code at +60s. They went straight into editing sweep.ts without articulating the expected behavior first, which cost several rounds of failed attempts.

The first edit at +60s came before any stated mechanism — just a reaction to the failing test. Only at +250s, after two failed edit cycles including an unrelated detour into holds.ts, did they name the actual mechanism (releasing original count instead of remaining). That correct hypothesis came very late relative to the editing already done.

There are only three narrated lines across seven minutes (+30s, +250s, +400s), with long silent stretches of editing and test runs in between (e.g. +60s-+200s covering three file edits and two test runs with no narration). An interviewer would have had to interrupt repeatedly to know what was being tried and why.

The candidate edited sweep.ts at +60s, then pivoted to holds.ts at +160s without any stated rationale connecting it to a hypothesis, then returned to sweep.ts at +280s and +340s. This is a scattered pattern — an edit to a file (holds.ts) unrelated to the eventual root cause, followed by two more attempts in sweep.ts before landing on the fix, without narrating why each attempt failed or what changed between them.

They ran the test suite after every single edit (+100s, +200s, +320s, +390s) rather than declaring success prematurely, and only stopped once the suite passed at +390s. This is a solid, if mechanical, verification habit — rerun-until-green rather than assuming success.

The closing line at +400s connects the fix to the mechanism (remaining count vs original count) rather than treating the pass as magic, echoing the hypothesis stated at +250s. It is brief and not deeply elaborated on why the phantom stock occurred, but it does tie fix to cause.
